clues: This city sits on the north coast of an island off the west coast of Africa. It belongs to the north province of that island, Bioko.
The wet season lasts nine long months, from March to November. A short dry season then runs from December to February, and January is the driest month.
This city served as the capital of its land for many years. In early 2026, a new city took that role from it at last.
Spanish is the state tongue here, but day to day talk often uses Pichinglis. It is a creole tongue used to chat and trade all across the island.
This is the oldest city in its whole land. Its streets have seen more years than those of any other city there.
